Subject: Bulk export of audit + access logs for regulatory review

Hi Rishi,

We're preparing for a scheduled regulator review in May and need a bulk extract of tenant audit logs (admin events + access traces) for our account for the period 2027-10-01 to 2028-03-31. Primary asks: residency of exported data (EU vs US), export formats (NDJSON / Parquet), estimated time to produce, and whether the export process can preserve a tamper-evident manifest (checksums + signed manifest). Also need clarity on whether the exported data counts as a separate retention copy and how deletion is handled afterward.

Can you confirm options and timeline? I attached a short requirements spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of IT Compliance, Finvero

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Bulk export of audit + access logs for regulatory review

Olivia — thanks for the note and the sheet, that helps. High level answers first:

- Residency: we can export data to either an EU-hosted, S3-compatible bucket (eu-west-1) or to a US-hosted bucket (us-east-1). For your EU residency requirement we recommend eu-west-1; exports are written directly from the Private control plane for your tenant so data never routes through our public hosted analytics pipeline.

- Formats: we support NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and Apache Parquet. NDJSON is the default for audit events (one event per line) and is easiest for manual review. Parquet is available for large extracts and is more efficient for analytics.

- Tamper-evident manifest: we produce a manifest.csv with filename, object-size, sha256 checksum and a manifest signature token. For higher-assurance needs we can provide a signed PKCS7 envelope; that is an ops request and needs 48-72 hours prep.

- Retention / deletion: exports are a customer-managed copy. By default we do not retain a separate Redwood copy beyond the export operation unless you request short-term staging (48 hours) to allow re-hydration. If you opt-in to staging we will keep a transient copy for the specified window and then run an erase job; we provide certificate-of-deletion on request.

Next steps I recommend: schedule a 30-minute call to confirm the export scope (events, tenants, time window) and choose format + destination. Karthik, can your team estimate scheduling and runbook steps? Monica — we'll need the ops runbook and a draft manifest example we can share with Finvero.

— Rishi

Signature: Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Looping in ops. Quick notes from schedule/planning:

- Rough lead time: 5 business days for NDJSON export to eu-west-1 if no staging is required. Parquet exports can take longer (7–10 business days) because we run a chunked compaction phase for large time ranges.

- Cost & throttling: large tenants may incur egress charges for cross-region; if Finvero keeps export in eu-west-1 there is no cross-region egress.

- Legal hold: if Legal Ops requests a legal hold for the export window, that will create an override that prevents deletion of records in the primary store; we can still export but deletion certificates are delayed until hold is lifted. Need confirmation from Finvero Legal.

- Post-export erase: ops can run an erase playbook to wipe any transient staging. We produce an export manifest and a checksum file per object.

Monica, can you assemble: (1) a sample manifest (CSV) and (2) the ops steps we run (S3 bucket policy, KMS envelope if requested, restart/resume steps for long exports)?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Attaching the runbook excerpts and a sample manifest. I included an example manifest row in the email below and a note about verification steps.

Attachment: sample_manifest_ndjson_manifest.csv (CSV, 4KB)

Sample manifest row (CSV columns: object_key, size_bytes, sha256, utc_timestamp):
finvero/2027-10-01/0001.ndjson, 124572, 9b7f2b8c4d1a..., 2028-04-10T16:20:11Z

Verification steps we run:
1) Export job writes into a dedicated export prefix in the requested region.
2) Post-write, the exporter computes per-object sha256 and writes manifest.csv.
3) Ops runs a checksum verification job (parallel) to validate manifest entries.
4) If requested, we sign the manifest with our ops PKI and package as PKCS7 envelope (this requires a maintenance window 48–72 hours earlier).
5) If staging was requested we schedule a delete job 48 hours after confirmation; the delete job produces an audit of objects deleted and a tombstone report.

Note on residency: for eu-west-1 exports we use customer-controlled S3 bucket policies and KMS keys that are region-scoped. We do not export through a US intermediate.

I can share the full runbook link once Rishi confirms schedule.

— Monica
